name: Cecil Hassan
life: “I still remember showing a scar I usually hid with my hand.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Cecil by a small Saturday habit. Cecil pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I used to dye my fringe to hide a scar. I came to have the scar shown for the first time.
appearance: Cecil has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for short black hair swept back. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a long navy raincoat with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead. In conversation Cecil folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Cecil takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Cecil can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To wear the scar openly after the trim.
family: Celia Lai is Cecil’s stepsibling. Cecil brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Celia checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The button card*, Celia says, “I need an enormous button I can close with one useful thumb.”
connections: Loretta Lu. A client revealing a scar provides a child with a braver explanation for the chair.
